records.reason: m81 under pure EA at 55.5 mg adds the missing low-loading baseline. Recent e301272fe83481e8a85d and da1432805cdb94057366 finished at 14.64 and 6.96 mL at 111 and 166.5 mg, while current predictions remain nearly loading-invariant. This third level distinguishes a gradual response from a localized loading transition.

This eligible exact repeat of m81 under pure EA at 111 mg checks the 14.64 mL completion in e301272fe83481e8a85d. Its current prediction remains about 10.48 mL. Reproducibility is needed before assigning the strong loading contrast to a deterministic structure-condition relationship.

m81 at 2/1 and 55.5 mg connects measured low-loading 1/1 and 5/1 records fa5d86f56c1c38fa9416 and 904c7849feb1c686924a, which finished at 13.71 and 18.80 mL. The predicted 9.46 mL completion tests whether an intermediate minimum exists or the low-loading curve remains compressed.

Other high-loading observations support short early completion, but current prediction is about 9.84 mL. The repeat separates stable endpoint-specific loading information from label variability.

Same-ratio 111 mg observation db2709229820b71e283b supplies a loading reference for this possible convergence.

m33 at 1/1 and 49.85 mg tests loading transfer of the confirmed early completion decline. Same-loading pure-EA record 17fd49e7bf1b8c8b08f7 finished at 12.53 mL, whereas the 99.7 mg pure-EA/1/1 pair 915cf3a7c8100cb7ce1f and 7a9775ac62acbc27a73d declined from 17.03 to 15.02 mL.

m33 at 5/1 and 149.55 mg pairs with the selected 2/1 point and compares directly with 99.7 mg record 3b45c013164f91745fd2, measured at 5.53/11.67 mL. It tests whether the newly confirmed completion minimum transfers across loading independently of onset.

m115 under pure EA at 162 mg supplies a matched baseline for recent 1/1 and 2/1 records aa4c0f940c011630a345 and d1ea63515e645b84e0cd, finishing at 18.08 and 21.62 mL. The unexpectedly long pure-EA completion of sulfur analogue m128 in d2d36d9586f3f49acd5d makes baseline transfer worth testing.

Ortho-methoxy ketone m127 under pure EA at 109 mg is predicted to finish at 14.79 mL, above same-loading 1/1 observation b688bf34f76e0d26985a at 9.86 mL. This tests an uncovered baseline decline after analogous large m29/m38 predictions failed, while allowing a genuine compound-specific decline.

m127 at 2/1 matches the selected pure-EA row and measured 1/1 record b688bf34f76e0d26985a. Predicted completion rebounds to 17.74 mL with a large quantile span. This three-condition comparison distinguishes a local minimum from baseline or slope errors in a methoxy-carbonyl environment.

Dimethoxy aromatic ether m116 under pure EA at 105.1 mg begins a controlled 0/1–1/1–2/1 experiment. Its predicted 7.53/13.75 mL endpoints are later than the selected 1/1 predictions. The only supplied early measured anchor, 59752d0b8c96b9efb90c at 2/1 and 52.55 mg, does not establish this decline.

m116 at 1/1 and 105.1 mg matches the selected pure-EA and 2/1 rows. Predicted completion falls from 13.75 to 9.56 mL before rising at 2/1. Measuring the middle point tests the proposed minimum without confounding loading solvent, loading volume or sample amount.

m116 at 2/1 completes the fixed-loading early curve and tests transfer from lower-loading observation 59752d0b8c96b9efb90c, measured at 6.88/10.43 mL. Together, the three labels distinguish a baseline artifact, a genuine completion minimum and a loading-dependent response.

Trimethoxy aromatic ether m110 at 1/1 and 112.6 mg fills an uncovered early region with high CW distance and a broad V2 quantile span. It forms a controlled pair with the selected 2/1 point; measured pure-EA and 2/1 references 3ba72d7e71d02ea168dd and 7c9b7238a83ed646815a are at lower loading.

m110 at 2/1 matches the selected 1/1 conditions. Predicted completion declines from 12.90 to 10.48 mL while onset also decreases. The pair tests whether adding a third methoxy group changes the early curve relative to m116, rather than transferring a descriptor-level polarity correction.

Dialdehyde m191 at 1/1 and 100 mg probes the highest-CW early region. Predicted completion is 23.69 mL, above measured 21.00 mL at 2/1 in acdffd73c7b1388ba321, while pure-EA record 141a4d64a7d140eefdc3 finished at 13.54 mL. This tests an early overshoot versus smooth growth.

m191 under pure EA at 150 mg anchors the selected high-loading 1/1 row and measured 2/1 record 53becf1a41d72abcc45a. Comparison with 100 mg pure-EA observation 141a4d64a7d140eefdc3 tests baseline loading transfer before interpreting the two selected 1/1 completions.

m191 at 1/1 and 150 mg forms a loading contrast with the selected 100 mg row and a ratio contrast with the selected pure-EA baseline. Predicted completion changes little with loading, whereas measured 2/1 endpoints in 53becf1a41d72abcc45a and acdffd73c7b1388ba321 differ. This tests endpoint-specific transfer.

Phenylmalonate m75 at 1/1 and 109.5 mg supplies a matched baseline for the selected 2/1 row. Recent lower-loading 7d65ab8e0e7b962da35f measured 5.29/7.84 mL, followed by the nearly zero-width 2/1 interval in f2312f90dd4cf5ef0e23. The pair tests whether that exceptional early transition transfers across loading.

m75 at 2/1 and 109.5 mg tests transfer of the 12.58/12.61 mL interval measured at 54.75 mg in f2312f90dd4cf5ef0e23. Current prediction itself reverses the endpoints slightly. The selected 1/1 row and measured same-loading 5/1 record f82f2844c7e27afd32bb constrain the response around this exceptional point.

m75 at 5/1 and 54.75 mg directly follows the recent narrow 2/1 record f2312f90dd4cf5ef0e23 at fixed conditions. The model predicts earlier onset and similar completion. This tests whether the apparent onset maximum is localized, and connects to later same-loading measurements ce3b9d9cbe1699c7eef9 and 3726956d81fe3954e5b7.

Long-chain acrylate m18 at 1/1 and 88.4 mg has an inverted prediction, 8.06/1.72 mL. Same-loading pure-EA and 2/1 records d997636736faa38ac83a and b8c5b2ddf2469922c305 have ordinary ordered intervals. This missing intermediate label directly tests the learned endpoint curve in a low-polarity ester family.

Branched acrylate m16 at 1/1 and 88.5 mg also has an inverted prediction, 6.86/6.22 mL. Its amount and loading-solvent volume nearly match selected m18, although the loading solvents differ and remain explicit. Later m16 observations 66f42d226a5f7e934a86 and 97fe38c6942b67ea70b2 provide ordered reference intervals.

The loading contrast tests whether any baseline correction is transferable across amounts, following the structure-specific loading associations measured for m81 and m33.

Salicylaldehyde m197 under pure EA at 114.6 mg fills the remaining baseline before same-loading 1/1 and 2/1 records 69be7348f9ab10739164 and 454eb2207b9abc0b2a6d, both finishing near 25 mL. Predicted pure-EA completion is 13.08 mL. This locates the strong-eluent transition after the proposed deep 2/1 dip failed.

Methoxy-substituted salicylaldehyde m117 under pure EA at 121.43 mg supplies a baseline matched to 2/1 observation 5079d0dfcde65893b224, measured at 4.88/15.80 mL. Together with selected m197, it tests substituent-dependent donor-carbonyl baselines while retaining their different loading solvents and volumes.

Methyl salicylate m105 at 1/1 and 117.4 mg begins a matched early pair after pure-EA observation bc780f413159cf9913d4, measured at 4.39/10.31 mL. The predicted completion stays near 10 mL, contrasting with m197's measured long 1/1 completion. This tests functional-group transfer within an ortho donor-carbonyl environment.

m105 at 2/1 matches the selected 1/1 conditions and pure-EA record bc780f413159cf9913d4. Predicted onset decreases slightly while completion increases. The pair resolves endpoint-specific response for the phenol ester and provides a chemical comparison to the now-measured growing early curves of m89 and m104.

Ortho-nitro aldehyde m198 under pure EA at 100 mg anchors the selected 1/1 row and measured 2/1 record 66178a861f4bf31fa2e1, which finished at 14.97 mL. It adds a non-donor, multiacceptor comparison to the phenol-carbonyl experiments and separates positional substitution from a generic polarity baseline.

m198 at 1/1 matches the selected pure-EA conditions and measured 2/1 record 66178a861f4bf31fa2e1. The predicted 13.93 mL completion nearly approaches the 2/1 endpoint. Measuring both early anchors tests whether this approach is real and whether nitro-aldehyde response transfers differently from phenolic and amino carbonyl rows.

hypotheses.content: m81 has a substantial association between loading and early completion: the 166.5 mg records finish earlier than several lower-loading records under pure EA through 5/1, with much smaller onset differences. Recent pure-EA measurements strengthen the association, but its reproducibility and cause remain unresolved. At 10/1 the completion gap appears to narrow.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Current predictions still change little with loading despite several coherent completion contrasts. New loading levels and repeats can teach an endpoint-specific ratio-by-loading relationship without extending it to every ester or assuming a universal loading mechanism.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the pure-EA 111 mg and 1/1 166.5 mg repeats reproduce their contrasting completions? Where does the low-loading 2/1 response lie, and does the gap remain small at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: m33's early completion decline is measured at 99.7 mg: completion falls from pure EA through 1/1 to 5/1 before increasing at 10/1, while onset remains early. Other loading levels show different pure-EA and 1/1 completions, so the extent and location of the minimum should remain loading-specific.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This is a useful counterexample to imposing monotonic completion or moving V1 and V2 together. Additional amounts and intermediate ratios can teach where the measured decline transfers and where a separate loading correction is needed.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 149.55 mg curve retain short completion at both 2/1 and 5/1, and does the 49.85 mg pure-EA-to-1/1 curve decline at all?

hypotheses.content: The earlier possibility that pronounced predicted early completion dips would reproduce across several compounds is weakened. m29 and m38 instead showed growth, m197 lacked the predicted deep 2/1 minimum, and the selected amino-esters rose. Genuine declines in m33 and m164 mean analogous uncovered ether, methoxy-ketone and acrylate curves still require controlled measurements rather than a universal monotonic rule.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The latest failures were often baseline or response-shape errors rather than a uniform retention offset. Fixed-loading early curves can distinguish those errors and improve transfer among the many supplied neutral carbonyl, ether and ester rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which of the predicted m116, m127 and m110 minima are measured responses? Does m15's long pure-EA completion reproduce across loading, and does m115 retain its predicted short high-loading pure-EA baseline?

hypotheses.content: For m191, the predictor proposes long 1/1 completion with early onset and little completion change between 100 and 150 mg. This may represent a useful endpoint-specific early response or an overshoot in an uncovered condition region. The feature has not been established by measurement.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The 1/1 rows have the largest CW distances in the supplied pool and broad single-predictor quantile spans. Controlled labels around existing pure-EA and 2/1 anchors can teach the early response of a molecule with two carbonyl groups and distinguish loading effects on the two endpoints.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Is completion at 1/1 above, near or below the measured 2/1 endpoints, and does the 100-to-150 mg contrast agree at both pure EA and 1/1?

hypotheses.content: The nearly zero-width m75 interval measured at 2/1 and 54.75 mg may be a localized reproducible response or an exceptional observation. It should not yet define the onset or width response at other amounts. The rejected large loading interpretation for m80 reinforces the need for discrimination rather than a shared malonate loading law.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The retrained predictor now transfers this narrow interval to another amount and slightly reverses its endpoints. A new loading-level pair and an adjacent same-loading ratio can prevent one exceptional label from determining an inappropriate family-wide response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the 109.5 mg 1/1-to-2/1 pair reproduce the delayed narrow interval, and does the 54.75 mg onset return earlier at 5/1?

hypotheses.content: Strong-eluent baselines and completion responses depend on the structural environment around donor and carbonyl groups. m197 retains completion near 25 mL at 1/1–2/1, whereas the selected ortho-amino esters have shorter growing early curves. Phenol esters, methoxy-substituted phenol aldehydes and ortho-nitro aldehydes provide discriminating comparisons. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding is a chemical prior, not a demonstrated explanation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: These labels can distinguish baseline differences from ratio slopes and improve positional and functional-group transfer beyond coarse polarity descriptors. Comparisons retain the recorded loading differences and do not attribute cross-molecule contrasts solely to a single substituent.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where do the m197 and m117 pure-EA baselines lie relative to their measured early curves? Does m105 grow through 1/1–2/1, and how does the non-donor m198 baseline approach its measured 2/1 endpoint?

hypotheses.content: The m18 and m16 predictions at 1/1 imply V2 below V1 and therefore inconsistent intervals under the target definitions. They may indicate a poorly learned early acrylate response. Because inconsistent measured labels exist elsewhere in the catalog, the new outcomes must be examined rather than replaced with an assumed ordering constraint.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct measurements at the inverted predictions can repair endpoint coupling and structure-condition transfer in relatively hydrophobic ester rows. The diagnostic is the inconsistent prediction itself, not a claim of calibrated epistemic uncertainty or an attempt to maximize retention.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m18 and m16 1/1 labels give ordinary ordered intervals connecting nearby measured conditions, or reveal another region of label inconsistency?

feedback_interpretation: The latest measurements substantially revise the early-curve interpretation. m29 completion increased from 7.99 mL under pure EA to 10.80 mL at 2/1, and m38 increased from 9.32 to 13.27 mL; their predicted large declines failed. m197 finished at 25.00 mL at 2/1, close to its 25.53 mL 1/1 value, then at 27.93 mL at 5/1, rejecting the proposed deep minimum. m89 increased from 11.40 to 14.22 mL at matched 1/1 and 2/1 settings, and m104's measured 1/1 completion of 9.98 mL precedes its 11.86 mL 2/1 endpoint. These outcomes weaken transferable dip interpretations. In contrast, m33's 99.7 mg curve confirms a real completion decline: 17.03 under pure EA, 15.02 at 1/1 and 11.67 at 5/1, followed by 19.32 at 10/1. m81's pure-EA completions of 14.64 and 6.96 mL at 111 and 166.5 mg strengthen its loading association; the 166.5 mg 10/1 completion of 17.42 mL shows subsequent convergence. Current predictions still largely flatten these loading contrasts, motivating repeats and new levels. m128's pure-EA result of 7.81/14.83 mL also exposed a baseline error, so related ketones need baseline anchors as well as slope labels. m185's 12.36 mL completion at 2/1 versus 19.86 at 5/1 places more growth after 2/1 than previously predicted. m183's 152.85 mg 20/1 result, 16.26/36.09 mL, showed opposing endpoint errors at acquisition, cautioning against a shared shift. The new m73 near repeat at 1/1 gave 4.89/10.59 mL instead of the older narrow late interval; its pure-EA records also differ in completion. This region remains variable and does not identify a cause, so it receives no additional rows in this batch. Finally, m75's 12.58/12.61 mL 2/1 interval warrants a local transfer test, while the earlier m80 large-loading-slope interpretation remains rejected. All cited errors are historical acquisition errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale: The 32 distinct eligible IDs cover 15 already observed molecules through specific local learning questions. Five m81 rows address a persistent completion-versus-loading mismatch, including two exact eligible repeats that check reproducibility. Three m33 rows extend the genuine early completion decline across loading. The methoxy ketone and ether experiments test still-unanchored baselines and predicted minima after recent measurements showed that many superficially similar reversals were artifacts. The m191 and m75 experiments use loading and ratio contrasts to distinguish endpoint-specific responses from transfer of exceptional observations. Acrylate rows directly examine physically inconsistent predictions and a related strong-eluent loading baseline. Phenol-carbonyl and nitro-aldehyde comparisons extend the revised early-response interpretation into related functional environments. Existing measured anchors reduce the need to acquire every ratio or repeat many weak-eluent variants already represented nearby. Multiple rows per molecule form controlled comparisons; no duplicate tuple is selected twice within this batch. Quantile spans are uncalibrated outputs of one predictor, CW distance describes coverage in the supplied gradient feature space, and V2 minus V1 is an elution interval width. The expected benefit is better separation of structural baselines, ratio response, loading interactions and label variability across numerous remaining Row candidates. Missing experimental variables limit causal interpretation, so the plan seeks useful predictive relationships without assigning unobserved mechanisms or optimizing the chromatography of the selected rows.
